payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism in sodium-flow systems. Its independently audited, corrected governing cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the relevant capacity benchmark; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.
